exact_accumulator.reason: the fault is entirely after the accumulator

int32_no_overflow.reason: K unchanged and inside the bound

pow2_scale_identity.reason: no-op under pow2 scales, so outputs stay bit-identical

real_scale_tolerance.reason: PREDICTED MISS. Rounding a scale to bf16 moves it by at most 2^-9 relative, about half an output spacing, so differences should land at 1 ulp and sit inside a tolerance of 1. If measurement confirms this, check 6 has a false negative for reduced scale precision at its stated tolerance, which is a finding about the tolerance and not about the implementation.

shared_operands.reason: operands untouched; asserted by the injector self-tests

token_level_risk.reason: token-level; P5 is layer-level and supplies no margins

F1_scale_in_bf16.note: Under power-of-two scales this fault is a no-op: a power of two is exactly representable in bfloat16, so casting the scale changes nothing. Its observability is therefore regime-dependent, and the pow2 column below says silent for that reason rather than because the check is weak.
F1_scale_in_bf16.pairing: Arm A is the reference on the original operands; arm B is the injected epilogue on those same operands.

real_scale_tolerance.reason: PREDICTED MISS at all_elements. An extra bf16 rounding costs at most half a spacing at that step, so the compounded error should stay at 1 ulp. Predicting a miss here is the point: if it does exceed 1 ulp, the tolerance is tighter than this reasoning.

F2_double_rounding.note: Under pow2 scales the intermediate is a power of two times an exact integer, representable in bf16 when the accumulator is, so the extra rounding is a no-op.
F2_double_rounding.pairing: Arm A is the reference on the original operands; arm B is the injected epilogue on those same operands.

pow2_scale_identity.reason: under pow2 scales both associations are exact

real_scale_tolerance.reason: fault produces no differing output element; excluded from the denominator, not credited as a detection

F3_scale_order.note: Measured unobservable in all three probed regimes: fp32 reassociation perturbs by about 2^-23 while bf16 rounds at 2^-8, roughly fifteen binades below resolution. Zero differing elements is arithmetic, not a broken injector. Every cell below is therefore silent BY CONSTRUCTION and must be excluded from detection-rate denominators; crediting check 6 with a pass here would be counting an unobservable fault as a detected one.
F3_scale_order.pairing: Arm A is the reference on the original operands; arm B is the injected epilogue on those same operands.

real_scale_tolerance.reason: PREDICTED MISS. Truncation instead of round-to-nearest costs at most one spacing, so differences should be exactly 1 ulp and inside the tolerance. Of the three predicted misses this is the most consequential: a wrong rounding mode is a real defect that a tolerance of one spacing cannot see.

F4_truncate_output.note: Under pow2 scales the product is exactly representable, so truncation and round-to-nearest agree and the fault is a no-op.
F4_truncate_output.pairing: Arm A is the reference on the original operands; arm B is the injected epilogue on those same operands.

exact_accumulator.reason: the injected arm reports the same integer accumulator; the fusion changes when the scale is applied, not the integer sum

pow2_scale_identity.reason: under pow2 scales the folded multiply is exact

real_scale_tolerance.reason: PREDICTED MISS where observable at all: a float reduction of scaled products differs from an integer reduction by well under an output spacing at these magnitudes

F5_fused_order.note: Marginal: 0, 2 and 0 differing elements across the three probed regimes. Whether any cell is testable depends on the regime actually run, so observability is recorded per run and cells with zero differing elements are excluded from denominators exactly as for F3.
F5_fused_order.pairing: Arm A is the reference on the original operands; arm B is the injected epilogue on those same operands.

exact_accumulator.reason: the arms report the wrapped INT32 value while acc_ref is the int64 exact value, so this check catches the wrap independently of check 2

int32_no_overflow.reason: this is the check's purpose: 16129*K exceeds 2^31 at the constructed K, so it must report the layer as unlicensed

lossless_fp32_entry.reason: the exact accumulator is far above 2^24, so lossless fp32 entry fails as well; two checks firing on one fault is expected and is not double counting

pow2_scale_identity.reason: A equals B, so outputs are bit-identical even though the accumulator is wrong; PREDICTED MISS in the sense that a bitwise output check cannot see a shared wrap

real_scale_tolerance.reason: same reason: identical arms, zero ulp distance, while the computed values are wrong. This is the clearest demonstration that output agreement is not correctness

shared_operands.reason: both arms hold the same overflow-inducing operands

F6_int32_overflow.note: K is raised until 16129*K exceeds 2^31, so the accumulator wraps. Both arms are correct implementations on those operands, so A equals B; what must fire is the precondition machinery, not an A/B comparison.
F6_int32_overflow.pairing: Both arms are the correct implementation on the precondition-violating operands, so A and B agree by construction. These faults do not create an A/B difference; they create a situation checks 2 and 3 must report. acc_ref is always the int64 exact accumulator, so a wrapped arm differs from it.

exact_accumulator.reason: no wrap, so the arms match the exact reference

int32_no_overflow.reason: K is chosen to stay inside the INT32 bound, so this check must NOT fire; a fire here would mean the two precondition checks are not separable

lossless_fp32_entry.reason: max|acc| exceeds 2^24, which is exactly what it tests

shared_operands.reason: both arms hold the same operands

F7_above_2p24.note: K raised so max|acc| exceeds 2^24 while staying below 2^31: no wrap, but the universal lossless-fp32-entry guarantee is gone.
F7_above_2p24.pairing: Both arms are the correct implementation on the precondition-violating operands, so A and B agree by construction. These faults do not create an A/B difference; they create a situation checks 2 and 3 must report. acc_ref is always the int64 exact accumulator, so a wrapped arm differs from it.

F8_null.note: The false-positive control. Injector self-tests already assert the output is bit-identical to the reference, so every cell must be silent. Any fire is a false positive and is reported as such.
F8_null.pairing: Arm A is the reference; arm B is a semantics-preserving rewrite of it. Any check that fires is reporting a difference that does not exist.

exact_accumulator.reason: different operands give different accumulators, so this fires as a consequence of the operand difference and NOT as evidence of its own sensitivity

lossless_fp32_entry.reason: magnitudes stay inside 2^24 at the original K

F9_operand_mismatch.note: Added by A-10.2 because none of the original eight faults made the arms' operands differ, leaving check 1's detection rate untestable. Under this fault the other checks' verdicts say nothing about their detection ability: once operands differ, their premise is gone, and the report must label them accordingly.
F9_operand_mismatch.pairing: Arm A is the reference on the original operands; arm B is the reference on the modified operands. This is the only fault where the arms legitimately hold different operands.

governance: Pre-registration A-10 fixes the catalogue and the requirement that every cell carry a written prediction; A-10.2 adds F9; A-10.3 replaces the magnitude ladder with a coverage ladder and requires that a fault with zero differing output elements be reported as unobservable rather than as a check insensitivity.

pairing_rules.epilogue: Arm A is the reference on the original operands; arm B is the injected epilogue on those same operands.
pairing_rules.null: Arm A is the reference; arm B is a semantics-preserving rewrite of it. Any check that fires is reporting a difference that does not exist.
pairing_rules.operand: Arm A is the reference on the original operands; arm B is the reference on the modified operands. This is the only fault where the arms legitimately hold different operands.
pairing_rules.precondition: Both arms are the correct implementation on the precondition-violating operands, so A and B agree by construction. These faults do not create an A/B difference; they create a situation checks 2 and 3 must report. acc_ref is always the int64 exact accumulator, so a wrapped arm differs from it.

predicted_misses: Cells marked PREDICTED MISS expect a real defect to pass a check. They are pre-registered deliberately: F1, F2, F4 and F5 against check 6, and F6 against checks 5 and 6. If measurement contradicts them, the reasoning stated in the cell is what was wrong.
reading_rule: A predicted should_fire that stays silent is a false negative. A predicted should_not_fire that fires is a false positive. A cell whose fault produced zero differing output elements in the run is excluded from both denominators and reported separately.
scope: P5 measures the sensitivity of checks 1 to 6. Check 7 is token-level and tolerance-based; a layer-level injection supplies no margins or flips, so it is marked not_applicable in all nine rows and its sensitivity is NOT measured by P5. That gap is stated here rather than hidden behind a count of seven.
status: PRE-REGISTERED. Written and hash-pinned before any P5 measurement.
